plain_description.what: A positive control for the split certificate. It merges two distinct declared MMLU-Pro subjects into one cell, at strong, medium and borderline pairings. Then it asks whether the certificate detects the known two-way split at realistic sizes (about 450-490 questions). No calls.
plain_description.why: An earlier test saw 0 of 60 two-way splits certified. That could mean no real structure, or a certificate too weak to see two-way structure. A known-strength control would tell these apart.
plain_description.information: If known two-way splits certify, the certificate can see that kind of structure. If they fail at full size, the certificate has a sensitivity limit. Result: done, a non-outcome. No chosen pair qualified as a valid control. Only chemistry+law certified, and only by a margin smaller than its own subsampling noise. So the certificate's sensitivity to two-way splits stays undetermined. This does not show the certificate is too strict or insensitive.
